title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a compact (here oriented) surface carrying a 'carte triangulaire', i.e. a map all of whose faces are triangles. A 'pondération' (weighting) is a labelling of the vertices by {0,1,∞} such that each face receives all three labels. Equivalently, X with the triangulation is pulled back from the standard two-triangle decomposition of P^1 (upper and lower half-planes) by a map ramified only over 0,1,∞, that is, a Belyi-type map whose dessin is this triangulation. The previous page builds a ramified S_3-principal covering X' → X from the flags of the barycentric subdivision. Its fibre over a face is the set of bijections {vertices of the face} → {0,1,∞}, an S_3-torsor. Crossing an edge identifies the torsors of the two adjacent faces: the two shared vertices keep their labels and the third label is forced. A weighting is then the same thing as a global section.

This page.
(1) Ramification. If the triangular structure is 'strict' (no monogons, no folded edges), the only possible extra ramification of X' → X is at the vertices. Around a vertex v of order n, the monodromy is τ^n, where τ is the transposition of the two labels other than v's. So X' is ramified at v iff n is odd.
(2) Étaleness. Suppose all faces are triangles, there are no folded edges or monogons, and all vertex orders are even; these are necessary conditions for weightability. Then X' → X is an unramified S_3-torsor, and weightings correspond bijectively to its global sections ('sauf erreur').
(3) Oriented refinement. In a weighted oriented triangulation, each face is + or − according to whether its cyclic order 0→1→∞ agrees with the orientation, and adjacent faces get opposite colours. So a 2-colouring of the faces is necessary. Such colourings correspond to sections of the ±1-torsor X'/A_3 obtained by pushing out along sgn: S_3 → {±1}.
(4) Next page. A chosen colouring reduces the structure group to A_3 ≅ Z/3. This gives a Z/3-torsor X'^+ → X with class cl(X) ∈ H^1(X, Z/3). Its vanishing is necessary and sufficient for a weighting with the prescribed + faces, and such weightings correspond to sections of the torsor.

Purpose. The page gives a cohomological criterion for when a triangulated surface is a 'pondered' (Belyi / equilateral) triangulation. It belongs to the Teichmüller / dessins d'enfants programme: these are the cartes coming from P^1 − {0,1,∞} together with its S_3 symmetry.
errors: Grammatical slip: 'dans le revêtement X'' and 'dans le revêtement associé de X est non ramifié' should read 'alors le revêtement…'.
The sentence beginning 'Comme tous les ordres des sommets sont pairs' is really a hypothesis ('Donc si tous les ordres…').

For X' to be unramified one also needs the absence of monogons (ramification at face centres), which is implicit in 'faces sont des triangles'. Grothendieck lists 'pas d'arêtes pliées' explicitly but not the monogon condition in the second sentence.
Otherwise the monodromy argument (τ^n around a vertex of order n) is correct.

ideas.what: S_3-torsor (local system) over a triangulated surface whose sections are the 3-colourings of vertices with each face receiving all three colours; ramified exactly at odd-degree vertices (plus degenerate faces/edges)
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy / group of projectivities of a triangulation; balanced (3-colourable) triangulations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heawood (1898, sphere case: 3-colourable iff all degrees even); S. Fisk (1970s, geometric colouring theory); M. Joswig (2002, group of projectivities)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses cartes, dessins and S_3 symmetry, but this explicit torsor criterion does not appear there as far as I know

ideas.what: Oriented case: face 2-colouring as a section of the sign-pushed ±1-torsor; reduction to A_3 = Z/3 yields an obstruction class cl(X) ∈ H^1(X, Z/3) to weightability
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological obstruction to 3-colouring of vertices of a triangulated surface / to existence of an equilateral (Belyi) triangulation structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fisk; Joswig; later Izmestiev and coauthors (holonomy of triangulations)

ideas.what: Weightings of triangulations ↔ maps to P^1 branched over {0,1,∞} (equilateral triangulations), with S_3 acting on weightings
ideas.modern_name: Dessins d'enfants / Belyi maps; Shabat–Voevodsky equilateral triangulations

missed.claim: Grothendieck's S_3-torsor of local weightings is exactly what combinatorialists later called the group of projectivities / colouring monodromy of a triangulation. His Z/3 obstruction class links this combinatorial colouring theory (Heawood–Fisk–Joswig) with dessins d'enfants and Belyi maps. The two literatures seldom cite each other, and this 1981 formulation predates Joswig.
missed.quote: il y a ramification en un sommet de X sss celui-ci est d'ordre impair … Les sections correspondent 1-1 aux pondérations de la structure triangulaire sur X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean torsor/cohomological criterion for when a triangulated surface carries a Belyi map with that triangulation as its 'clean' dessin. That could be useful in enumerating equilateral triangulations and in studying the Galois action on them.

missed.claim: For oriented triangulated surfaces, an explicit obstruction cl(X) ∈ H^1(X, Z/3), relative to a chosen face 2-colouring, vanishes iff a weighting exists. Weightings with that colouring are then a torsor under H^0 of the Z/3 local system. This is credited in the colouring literature to Fisk and Joswig, not to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: Les coloriages correspondent aux sections du fibré X'/S_3^+ associé au fibré en groupes S_3, par S_3 → ±1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point only; the mathematics itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: The result is correct and elegantly framed as a torsor, but its combinatorial content (even degrees, monodromy of 3-colourings, Z/3-type obstruction) is known from Heawood, Fisk and Joswig. What is mildly notable is Grothendieck's independent cohomological formulation inside the dessins programme around 1981.
transcription_corrections: 'dans le revêtement X'' and 'dans le revêtement associé' probably read 'alors le revêtement'.
'Comme tous les ordres des sommets sont pairs' is probably 'Donc si tous les ordres des sommets sont pairs'.
'On peut décrire encore un peu plus' may be 'On peut détailler encore un peu plus'.
The interlinear insertion above 'stricte' reads 'triangulaire'; the insertion above 'triangulaire' in line 9 reads 'de carte'.
Last line: 'dans une restriction' is more likely 'dans une réduction' (of the structure group), consistent with the next page.
